$comment: The macOS 27 dark-standard material: the difference document, in the same
relationship to the runtime default that apple-macos-26.5-1x-dark-standard.json
is in. It serves both dark profiles, at both scales.
Read it against the 27 LIGHT document rather than against the 26.5 dark one for
what this child changed: the two schemes' refits are the same three laws at
different numbers, and the dark scheme keeps a thin/thick split at the bright end
of the response where the light scheme's rows converge.

measurement.fixtures: apps/reference-apple/fixtures/apple-macos-27.0-1x-dark-standard-glass0.5 and -2x-, the W29 G1 bed at seven runs per cell, slider 0.5
measurement.fixtureSets: calibration and probe; validation checked and never fitted; holdout read once at the sealed configuration
measurement.webCell: chromium 151.0.7922.34, renderer webgpu, samplingBackend gpu-texture, adapter apple/metal-3

method: The same reading as the light document's, and it is the same statement about
the material rather than about the scheme: over `dark-solid` the 27 dark
reference settles at 0.0419 against a backdrop of 0.011 linear, four times it,
and over `impulse` at 0.0356 against 0.0003. Nothing on this bed converges on
its backdrop, so the band that made the material converge stands down.
Four knots, as the light document's, and the third at 0.47 rather than 0.425:
the dark bed's two structured backdrops sit at 0.425 and 0.500 and read within
0.04 of each other, so one knot between them carries both and the gated cells
are `photo` and `checkerboard`.
The ordinates are the reference's own levels, corrected once by the rendered
residual. The reference's dark level rose by about three times across the bed
— `photo__rrect-md__rest` 0.1887 against vitrea's 0.0415, `checkerboard`
0.1646 against 0.0498 — which is the same finding as the light scheme's, at a
scheme whose neutral is 0.05 rather than white.
Unlike the light scheme, the two rows do NOT converge at the bright end:
0.464 thin against 0.196 thick at 0.95, read off `light-solid__rrect-sm__rest`
(0.4721) and `light-solid__rrect-lg__rest` (0.2036). The dark material over a
bright backdrop still depends strongly on how thick the surface is.
The dark rim's amplitude law read the same way as the light one, and the
finding is in the GAIN: 2.334 was fitted on a body whose level ran 0.01 to 0.16,
and the 27 body runs 0.04 to 0.47, so the same gain would draw a rim four times
the reference's on the bright cells. The least-squares line through the five
backdrops' (level, wanted amplitude) pairs is 0.055 + 0.44 x — a larger
intercept and a fifth of the gain, which is the dark rim becoming much flatter
in the body's own level.
The width moves far less than the light scheme's: the dark reference's FWHM is
about 1.25 CSS px against vitrea's 1.0, so 2.2.
The dark document names no heavy tap (`sizeHeavyTapSigma` 0 at both scales, and
that is unchanged), so the mix is the whole lever here. Fitted on the interior's
spread with the level already refitted: the bed-wide signed residual is −0.014
at 0.34, and the per-backdrop spread is inside ±0.05 on every backdrop but
`checkerboard-64`.
The light document's constant, carried here so that one scheme's dom tier is
not blurred differently from the other's for want of a key. The dark dom tier
meets every adopted row at either value; it is set for coherence, not by a fit
of its own, and this entry says so.
